catalog_quote: 5. Stress. Stress is not a salient phonological phenomenon in Lamjung Yolmo. There are no observable perceptual cues for phonemic stress and it is only used by speakers as a strategy for lexical emphasis.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim at the stated place in the Gawne 2016 PDF we hold (printed p.39, PDF p.50; tone sec.3 p.33). (2) Deciding source: a 2016 sketch grammar (171 pp) by the language's principal documenter with a dedicated 'Stress' section; the identical statement is in her 2013 PhD grammar appendix (p.437, downloaded now), which is the Glottolog 'grammar' entry. No later or more specialised stress description exists in the Glottolog list; the one instrumental prosody study (Teo, Gawne & Baese-Berk 2015, downloaded) analyses only word-initial lexical tone plus phrasal intonation and never invokes stress, consistent with the no-word-stress coding and with the record's the primary-stress rule (binary H/L word tone on the first syllable). Gawne 2019 (downloaded) is silent on stress and repeats the word-initial tone statement. One nuance worth noting but not coding-changing: the 2013 thesis

sources.quote: Instrumental (F0) study of Lamjung Yolmo and Kagate: 'lexical tone is only specified at the left edge of the word, while the right edge of the word is free to take post-lexical intonation tones.' No mention of word stress; prosody analysed entirely as word-initial lexical tone plus phrasal intonation.
